program_meta.english_test: REQUIRED, C1 level, VERIFIED matching prior notes almost exactly. program_meta.advisor_model: UNUSUAL FOUR-INSTITUTION ECOSYSTEM, clarified this pass. The Saarland Informatics Campus (SIC) co-locates four legally separate institutions on one campus: (1) Saarland University Dept of Computer Science (degree-granting, where Akshat would enroll for MSc CS/DSAI), (2) Max Planck Institute for Informatics (MPI-INF, 6 departments incl. D2 Computer Vision and Machine Learning under Bernt Schiele), (3) Max Planck Institute for Software Systems (MPI-SWS), (4) DFKI (German Research Center for AI, applied/industry-facing). Many MPI-INF and MPI-SWS researchers ALSO hold adjunct/honorary professorships at Saarland University and formally supervise University theses and PhDs - this is the normal route, not an exception. MSc admission itself is to the University CS/DSAI program only (not to a specific advisor or institute) - there is no rotation system at MSc level. MPI-INF's own 'Bachelor and Master Theses' page (verified) confirms MPI-INF group leaders DO supervise Saarland University Bachelor's/Master's theses directly - i.e. an MSc CS student CAN reach an MPI-INF, MPI-SWS, or DFKI researcher for a thesis, but this happens by informal direct contact with the individual researcher/group AFTER enrollment, not through the admissions portal. PhD-level: MPI-INF D2 also runs open-ended 'Direct Applications' (email d2-application@mpi-inf.mpg.de anytime) plus formal joint programs (IMPRS-TRUST joint with MPI-SWS/Saarland/RPTU, deadlines 30 June & 31 Dec; CS@maxplanck; Maryland-Max-Planck program) that are separate from the University's own MSc/PhD admissions.
program_meta.ms_research_access: Yes, via direct contact after enrollment - confirmed by MPI-INF's dedicated 'Bachelor and Master Theses' page for D2 (Computer Vision and Machine Learning) and by MPI-INF group leaders being reachable at *.mpi-inf.mpg.de addresses. No centralized placement; the student contacts a specific professor/group leader directly once enrolled (or even before, informally) to arrange a Bachelor's/Master's thesis inside an MPI-INF/MPI-SWS/DFKI group while remaining formally enrolled at the University.
program_meta.notes: Semester fee: could not find an exact current EUR figure on the official 'Fees' hub this pass - the page confirms 'All students currently pay a semester fee, which comprises the student services fee, the administrative charge and the AStA fee. The semester fee also covers the cost of the semester travel ticket [Deutschlandticket-equivalent]' and links to a separate 'Fee amount' subpage that was not independently opened - GAP, the prior note's ~EUR395 figure is PLAUSIBLE (matches the general German public-university range and explicitly bundles a semester travel ticket as claimed) but UNVERIFIED this pass; re-check https://www.uni-saarland.de/en/study/organisation/fees/semester-fee.html directly. Tuition itself: NOT applicable for a first Master's degree ('If you are studying for a first degree or you are on a consecutive Master's degree programme, there are no tuition fees'). Minimum admission bar: cumulative undergraduate GPA of at least 75% (or 3.00/4.00) AND ranking in the top 10% of the graduating class - Akshat's 9.56/10 CGPA should clear the GPA bar comfortably; class rank must be separately confirmed/documented. Two MSc programs are both viable targets for Akshat and share one Application Guide: MSc Computer Science (broad, covers AI/ML/CV/cybersecurity/HCI/software engineering) and MSc Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (explicitly ML/AI/big-data/stats-focused, coordinated by Prof. Jens Dittrich, Databases group) - DSAI is likely the sharper fit given Akshat's data-centric-ML and uncertainty-quantification profile.
